title: The CEO’s Secret Wife
description: A contract marriage turns dangerous when hidden feelings become impossible to deny. Evelyn didn't expect to fall for the man she was paid to marry.

seasons.title: The Contract
seasons.description: How it all started with a single signature.

parts.text:
She stared at the thick, cream-colored contract lying on the mahogany desk. One signature. That was all it took to change the trajectory of her life forever. It wasn't just a piece of paper; it was a surrender of her freedom, a pact with a man who felt more like a myth than a human being.

Evelyn could feel the weight of her family's debts pressing down on her shoulders. The hospital bills, the mortgage, the constant fear of the bailiffs knocking on the door. This contract was the only way out, but the price was her autonomy for the next three hundred and sixty-five days.

Mr. Sterling didn't look like a savior. He stood by the window, his silhouette sharp against the city skyline. He looked like a predator who had finally cornered his prey, patient and lethal. He was known as the 'Ice King' of the business world, a man who built empires and crushed competition without blinking.

When he finally turned around, his eyes were as cold as the glass behind him. He didn't offer a smile, only a steady, unyielding gaze. He was perfectly tailored, perfectly poised, and perfectly dangerous. Every inch of him screamed power, the kind that didn't need to raise its voice to be heard.

"Sign it, Evelyn," he said, his voice like velvet over gravel, sending a shiver down her spine that she couldn't quite name. "And your family's debt vanishes within the hour. No more collection calls, no more worry. Your mother will get the best care money can buy, and your brother's tuition will be handled."

He walked closer, stopping just inches from the desk. The scent of expensive cologne and old money drifted toward her. "All I require is your presence. For one year, you are Mrs. Sterling in the eyes of the world. No questions, no deviations, and certainly no scandals."

Her hand trembled as she gripped the heavy fountain pen. The cold metal felt like a brand against her palm. Was this freedom, or just a more gilded cage than the one she had been living in? She looked up at him, searching for even a glimmer of warmth, but found only the calculated resolve of a businessman closing a deal.

She thought of her mother's pale face in the hospital bed, and her brother's dreams of university slipping away. With a sharp intake of breath, she pressed the nib to the paper. The ink flowed smoothly, black and final. As she finished the last loop of her name, she felt the invisible walls of her new reality closing in.

The penthouse was cold, despite the expensive heating system that hummed silently in the background. Or maybe it was just him. Everything in the apartment was marble, glass, and steel—beautiful, sterile, and entirely devoid of life. It was a museum of wealth, not a home.

Evelyn stood in the center of the vast living room, her small suitcase feeling like an intruder in this world of opulence. She looked at the floor-to-ceiling windows, the city lights below looking like scattered diamonds. She was at the top of the world, yet she had never felt smaller or more alone.

He smiled like a man who had already won, though the expression didn't reach his eyes. He poured two glasses of amber liquid, the ice clinking softly against the crystal. But she had no idea he was hiding the bigger secret, a reason for this marriage that went far beyond mere convenience or business strategy.

He handed her a glass, his fingers briefly brushing hers. The contact felt like an electric shock, sharp and unsettling. He was watching her, studying her reactions like a scientist with a new specimen. She took a sip, the liquid burning a trail down her throat, giving her a momentary surge of artificial courage.

"There's only one rule in this house," he whispered, leaning close enough for her to smell the faint scent of whiskey on his breath. The proximity was overwhelming, making it hard to think, hard to breathe. "Don't fall in love. With the lifestyle, with the attention, or especially... with me."

He set his glass down with a definitive click. "Your room is the second on the left. We have a breakfast meeting at eight sharp tomorrow. Dress accordingly." He turned and walked away without a second glance, leaving her standing in the silence of her new, expensive life.
